story: Southwestern Public Service Company (Xcel Energy in the Texas Panhandle) runs Pano AI smoke-detection cameras. The PUCT order approving its resiliency plan lists AI camera fire detections as a metric, and SPS's first annual report answers that line with a count of cameras installed. Separately, the PUCT wildfire plan rule and staff's pro forma treat cameras as suggested, while Pano asked for a minimum requirement. The Tribune reports eight of 160 utilities had complied at a House State Affairs hearing. Record items tx-2026-0191 and tx-2026-0192.
notes: Reachability. interchange.puc.texas.gov and ftp.puc.texas.gov both returned HTTP 402 to WebFetch on 2026-09-28 (both ftp PDFs were tried live). Every PUCT quote was checked character for character against the local snapshot the brief names, which is recorded on each claim as local_snapshot. Only whitespace was collapsed. For Interchange PDFs the served PDF text layer was used, and OCR artifacts were kept as found, e.g. "SPS' s" with a space. The Texas Tribune was fetched live and the article is up. Its verbatim text was matched against the local copy, including curly apostrophes. The three Xcel Energy Stories pages were fetched live. Their quotes came back through the fetch tool's extraction on two separate passes that agreed. They are not a raw byte copy, so confidence on those claims is medium. Pleading-paper line numbers. The SPS application testimony ends each line with a line number. Claim c27 spans one of those breaks, and the number 6 after "either" was dropped from the quote, as flagged on that claim. Every other application quote sits inside a single line. Scope. The 97 cameras (c41) are 'across its service territory', which is not a Texas count. The Xcel title in c46 is the only fetched line that ties the operating company to New Mexico and Texas. The 33 in c8 is 'cameras installed' and is never a detection count. The application's plan of 68 cameras (c23), the report's 33 installed and 34 projected (c8) and Baldridge's 97 (c41) come from three different documents and three different scopes. No model may sum, subtract or reconcile them. c47 and c48 are Colorado. Findings noticed but kept out of the claims. Ordering paragraph 8 of the order tells SPS to use 'the metrics and evaluation criteria described in Finding of Fact 48', but the metric list is Finding of Fact 49 and FoF 48 is about implementation flexibility. That is a citation error in the order itself, not a claim. Pano's comments were on the DRAFT pro forma, where the section was numbered 'Section 7, Operational Protocols'. In the final pro forma it is Section 4 and situational awareness is 4.5. The TDEM text comes from the native file in ZIP item 59053_19_1582214, and the brief gives the URL as 59053_19_1582215.PDF. The served text of that PDF was not available to compare. The full rule text does not contain the word camera, but that is an absence and is not claimed. c1 records the rule header's effective date in the form the header prints it (12/04/25) rather than converting it.

claims.text: The Texas wildfire mitigation plan rule, 16 TAC §25.60, carries the header marking effective 12/04/25 and project number P-56789.
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans
claims.document: PUCT substantive rule §25.60, Project 56789, rule text PDF

claims.text: The wildfire mitigation plan rule applies to every electric utility, municipally owned utility and electric cooperative that owns a transmission or distribution facility in Texas.
claims.quote: This section applies to each electric utility, municipally owned utility, and electric cooperative that owns a transmission or distribution facility in this state.
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans

claims.text: The rule asks each plan to describe inspections, including any use of geospatial or remote sensing technologies such as LiDAR or satellite, or risk-modeling tools.
claims.quote: description of the entity’s use of geospatial or remote sensing technologies (such as Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), satellite, etc.) or risk-modeling tools
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans

claims.text: The rule requires a detailed operations plan for reducing wildfire ignition and responding to wildfire, including any use of automated fault detection devices or programs.
claims.quote: A detailed operations plan for reducing the likelihood of wildfire ignition from the entity’s transmission and distribution facilities and responding to a wildfire in the entity’s wildfire risk area(s), including, if applicable, a description of the entity’s use of automated fault detection devices or programs
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans

claims.text: Under the rule, the deadline to intervene in a wildfire mitigation plan case is 30 calendar days from the date service of notice is complete.
claims.quote: the intervention deadline is 30 calendar days from the date service of notice is complete.
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans

claims.text: An entity with an approved wildfire mitigation plan must file an annual report on it by May 1st of each year, starting the year after approval.
claims.quote: An entity with an approved wildfire mitigation plan must file an annual report on its plan by May 1 of each year, beginning the year after the plan is approved.
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans

claims.text: The rule lets commission staff develop one or more pro forma wildfire mitigation plans.
claims.quote: Commission staff may develop one or more pro forma wildfire mitigation plans.
claims.source_title: 16 TAC §25.60, Transmission and Distribution Wildfire Mitigation Plans

rejected.finding: PUCT System Resiliency Plans page, SPS entry (https://www.puc.texas.gov/industry/electric/system-resiliency-plans/)
rejected.reason: Unreachable. WebFetch got HTTP 402 on the URL with and without the trailing slash, and the brief names no local snapshot for this page. Nothing from it was verified. The approval date is covered instead by the annual report (c10) and the order's filing receipt (c31).

Not checked. The tools available here can't list a directory (Read on the folder returns EISDIR), so the scout files could not be enumerated or named. Per the brief, findings that are not this story are rejected as 'not this story'. Findings that bear on this story are covered only if they match a claim above.

rejected.finding: Any statement that SPS has 97 AI cameras in Texas
rejected.reason: The Tribune says 97 cameras 'across its service territory'. It gives no Texas-only count, and SPS's service territory is described by Xcel as New Mexico and Texas (c46).

rejected.finding: Any statement that SPS reported 33 AI camera fire detections
rejected.reason: The annual report line under the detections metric reads 'Actual: 33 cameras installed'. That is a count of cameras, not detections (c8).

rejected.finding: A Texas camera total built from the application's 68, the report's 33 installed and 34 projected, or the Tribune's 97
rejected.reason: The figures come from three documents with different scopes and dates, and none of them states a combined total. Any sum or difference would be a number produced by a model.

rejected.finding: Colorado camera detections or deployment figures (Douglas County, twenty-one camera systems, 1.5 million acres) presented as Texas facts
rejected.reason: Both Xcel stories describe Colorado. They are kept only as Colorado claims (c47, c48).

rejected.finding: SPS annual report O&M estimate of $321,177.68 for AI cameras in 2026
rejected.reason: The served PDF text prints the sentence as 'estimated $321,177.68 in 0&M', with a zero for the letter O. Only the projection half, $463,646 and 44.36%, was carried into c17. The figure itself does appear in both the served and native text if a maintainer wants to add it with that OCR note.

rejected.finding: The order's Ordering Paragraph 8 as the source of the metric requirement
rejected.reason: Ordering Paragraph 8 cites 'Finding of Fact 48' for the metrics, but the metric list is Finding of Fact 49 and FoF 48 is about implementation flexibility. The metric claim cites FoF 49(j) and FoF 51 directly (c33, c34), and the citation error is recorded in notes.

rejected.finding: Live-page verification of the 16 TAC 25.60 rule PDF and the April 17th, 2026 PUCT release on ftp.puc.texas.gov
rejected.reason: The live fetch returned HTTP 402 for both. This is not a rejection of the claims. c1 to c7 and c38 were verified against the local snapshots the brief names, as recorded on each claim.
